name: BioGrid 2.0
description: Second-generation biological grid network that distributes living intelligence across interconnected nodes. Merges mycelial routing, neural mesh topology, and polyhedral energy scaffolding into a unified transmission fabric.

core_attributes.pattern: adaptive mesh routing, distributed energy balancing, living topology

scope.definition: Fraction of total network function maintained after random removal of 20% of nodes in a scale-free biological distribution network, compared to equivalent non-hierarchical grid.

evidence.source: Barabási & Albert (1999) 'Emergence of scaling in random networks', Science 286:509-512; Albert et al. (2000) 'Error and attack tolerance of complex networks', Nature 406:378-382.
cross_domain_examples: scale-free networks retain 0.85-0.97 connectivity after 20% random node removal vs 0.60 for random graphs
internet topology: scale-free distribution makes it robust to random failures but vulnerable to hub attacks
mycorrhizal networks: scale-free hub structure with few highly-connected trees supporting resilience

scope.falsifiability: If scale-free BioGrid networks show equivalent failure resilience to random-graph equivalents after node removal, scale-free architecture provides no resilience advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: Scale-free resilience to random failure comes at the cost of vulnerability to targeted hub attack (3% hub removal can fragment the network). Resilience is failure-mode-specific.
